AbstractText.Label: Objective
AbstractText.content: Osteoarthritis is a leading cause of disability for which there is no cure. Psychosocial-oriented treatments are underexplored. We developed and tested an intervention to build positive psychological skills (e.g., gratitude) to reduce osteoarthritis symptom severity, including pain and functioning, and to improve psychosocial well-being in patients with knee or hip osteoarthritis.

AbstractText.Label: Design
AbstractText.content: Two-arm randomized design with six-month follow-up.

AbstractText.Label: Setting
AbstractText.content: An academic Veterans Affairs Medical Center.

AbstractText.Label: Subjects
AbstractText.content: Patients aged 50 years or older with knee or hip osteoarthritis and pain ratings of 4 or higher.

AbstractText.Label: Methods
AbstractText.content: Patients (N = 42) were randomized to a six-week program containing positive skill-building activities or neutral control activities tailored to the patient population. Adherence was assessed by telephone each week. We assessed osteoarthritis symptom severity (WOMAC Osteoarthritis Index) and measures of well-being (positive affect, negative affect, and life satisfaction) at baseline and by telephone one, three, and six months after the program ended. We used linear mixed models to examine changes over time.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: The majority (64%) of patients completed more than 80% of their weekly activities. Patients in the positive (vs neutral) program reported significantly more improvement over time in osteoarthritis symptom severity (P = 0.02, Cohen's d = 0.86), negative affect (P = 0.03, Cohen's d = 0.50), and life satisfaction (P = 0.02, Cohen's d = 0.36).

AbstractText.Label: Conclusions
AbstractText.content: The study successfully engaged patients with knee or hip osteoarthritis in a six-week intervention to build positive psychological skills. Improving osteoarthritis symptom severity and measures of psychosocial well-being, the intervention shows promise as a tool for chronic pain management.
